title: Full-hand electrotactile feedback using electronic skin and matrix electrodes for high-bandwidth human–machine interfacing
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences
key_design_claim: Electronic skin on a finger drove a 32-channel stimulator and forearm matrix electrode so that seven subjects recognised contact position and sliding, demonstrating high-bandwidth full-hand feedback for prosthesis users.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated on the forearm, so the full dose is owed; the stimulator's ranges (0-10 mA, 50-5000 us, up to 400 Hz) are stated, but the delivered amplitude, pulse width, rate and pad size used with the subjects are not.

title: Selective Activation of Peripheral Nerve Fibre Groups of Different Diameter by Triangular Shaped Stimulus Pulses
obligation_rationale: This is an animal (non-human) peripheral nerve electrophysiology study using triangular-pulse anodal block to differentially recruit fiber diameters via exposed nerve electrodes with a custom pulse stimulator (5-30 V, 0.5-1 ms pulses via 0.1-0.3 uF condensers), so it owes device/stimulus parameters for the bench/animal setup but has no human delivered-dose values since no stimulus was delivered to human participants.

title: Tactile and Kinesthetic Presentation Using the Same Electrode Array: Evaluation of Tactile Presentation and EMS-Induced Thumb Movement
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current, pulse width/rate, and electrode geometry (8x8 array, 2.0mm diameter, 3.5mm spacing) reported here to reproduce the tactile vs. HiZ-modulated EMS kinesthetic conditions, since the paper's core contribution is a novel electrode-switching scheme distinct from device hardware ratings, which are not specified numerically.

title: Multidimensional electrocutaneous stimulation
key_design_claim: Intensity discrimination thresholds for a five-parameter electrocutaneous stimulus fell by up to 60% when stimuli varied along the delivered-energy gradient, which was used for intensity control in the VideoTact vision-substitution array.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated on the abdomen, so the full dose is owed; the electrode pin diameter and cluster area are stated, but the stimulus is parameterised by voltage, pulse width, pulse count and burst period without numeric values in the extracted text.

title: First Steps Towards Designing Electrotactons: Investigating Intensity and Pulse Frequency as Parameters for Electrotactile Cues
obligation_rationale: The paper reports individually calibrated, delivered amplitude (0-20 mA) and pulse width (70-200 us) ranges and a fixed 20 PPS pulse frequency used to elicit perceived urgency/annoyance/valence/arousal on the palm, so readers need these delivered stimulus bounds to interpret the psychophysical discriminability findings, though no device hardware ratings (compliance, max output, channel count) are specified.

title: Electrophysiological and psychophysical quantification of temporal summation in the human nociceptive system
venue: European Journal of Applied Physiology and Occupational Physiology
key_design_claim: Repeating sural-nerve stimuli (five 1 ms pulses at 200 Hz) at 2-3 Hz facilitated the nociceptive withdrawal reflex together with temporal summation of pain, giving an objective reflex marker and a psychophysical summation threshold.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated percutaneously over the sural nerve, so a non-display dose is owed; rectangular pulses, five consecutive 1 ms pulses at 200 Hz per train, are stated (confirmed by the reviewer), but electrode geometry and currents were not found in the extracted text. Recorded rate is the 200 Hz intra-train rate.

title: Output Power Computation and Adaptation Strategy of an Electrosurgery Inverter for Reduced Collateral Tissue Damage
obligation_rationale: This paper describes an electrosurgery inverter's power computation and impedance-adaptation strategy tested on ex vivo tissue and bench setups, not a stimulus delivered to human participants, so readers are owed device output ratings (390 kHz, 15-45W power range, GaN inverter) but no human dosimetry parameters.

title: Conductive block copolymer elastomers and psychophysical thresholding for accurate haptic effects
key_design_claim: A soft conductive block-copolymer in a stretchable concentric layout, with psychophysical thresholding, gave detection at currents as low as 6 uA, better localisation than dual electrodes, and pressure-to-vibration switching around 6 Hz across 10 participants.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated on the forearm, so the full dose is owed; currents (6-20 uA detection, 10-250 uA pain testing), frequencies (1-100 Hz), biphasic symmetric waveform and contact areas (509 mm2 serpentine concentric; 505 and 2217 mm2 comparators) are stated. Pulse width is not reported in the paper or its supplement (checked 2026-10-06). Stimulator: Siglent waveform generators driving BioPac STMISOLA. Recorded at the upper current and frequency.

title: Design of multi-pad electrotactile system envisioned as a feedback channel for supernumerary robotic limbs
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered pulse width, rate, amplitude range, and electrode geometry actually used in the thigh calibration experiments to reproduce or compare the sensory thresholds reported.

title: Psychometric evaluation of high-resolution electrotactile interface for conveying 3D spatial information
obligation_rationale: Readers need delivered current, pulse timing, electrode pad size/spacing and body site to replicate the psychophysical discrimination results and compare spatial/frequency resolution across studies.

title: Overview of the Methods and Applications of Electrodermal Activity Assessment and Its Relation with Electrotactile Feedback and Potential Use in Automated Calibration
obligation_rationale: As a conceptual review/hypothesis paper with no actual stimulation experiments performed, it owes no delivered stimulation parameters; it only surveys EDA signal processing methods and proposes future work linking EDA to electrotactile calibration.

title: A High-Voltage Bidirectional Current Source
obligation_rationale: This is a bench power-electronics paper on current-source circuit design tested only into a resistive load, not on human subjects, so it owes readers device envelope specs (compliance voltage, max current, bandwidth) rather than delivered stimulation parameters.

title: Aβ-CT Affective Touch: Touch Pleasantness Ratings for Gentle Stroking and Deep Pressure Exhibit Dependence on A-Fibers
obligation_rationale: This paper uses mechanical touch (brushing, pressure, vibration) and nerve blocks rather than electrical stimulation, so it owes readers no electrotactile device or dosing parameters, only the mechanical/nerve-block protocol details already given.

title: Tactile displays: Overview and recent advances
obligation_rationale: As a review summarizing others' tactile-display and electrotactile stimulation implementations (e.g., SmartTouch's 1.0-3.0 mA, 0.2 ms pulses via 1 mm stainless steel electrodes), it owes readers accurate reporting of the cited device specs as rated/reported ranges rather than as stimuli delivered by this paper itself, since no original human stimulation was performed here.

title: Wearable High Voltage Compliant Current Stimulator for Restoring Sensory Feedback
obligation_rationale: This paper reports device-rated envelope specs (25 mA at 3.6 kΩ, ±90 V compliance, 4 channels) validated only on resistive/RC bench loads, not on humans, so readers need the rated capability and load-test conditions rather than any delivered dose.

title: Tactile innervation densities across the whole body
obligation_rationale: This is a review synthesizing innervation density and receptive-field data from prior neurophysiology studies; it delivers no stimulation to humans and owes no stimulus parameters, only citation-traceable density/receptive-field estimates.

title: A Portable, Arbitrary Waveform, Multichannel Constant Current Electrotactile Stimulator
obligation_rationale: This paper only characterizes the device against resistive bench loads (no human participants), so it owes readers the device's rated output envelope (±15 mA at ±150 V compliance, <2 µs rise time) rather than any delivered human stimulation parameters.

title: Preferential C-nociceptor stimulation facilitates peripheral axon reflex flare, but not secondary mechanical hyperalgesia
key_design_claim: 25 ms half-sine pulses (C-fibre-preferring) needed less current than 500 us rectangular pulses to reach pain NRS 6 (3.6 vs 9.2 mA, both 2 Hz) and produced larger axon-reflex flare, but not larger secondary hyperalgesia.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated intracutaneously, so the full dose is owed; a comparison of 25 ms half-sine (3.6 mA mean at NRS 6) and 500 us rectangular (9.2 mA) pulses, both 2 Hz alternating polarity, recorded as two delivered configurations. The active electrode area is not given, so charge density is unrecoverable; half-sine charge is about 64% of the rectangular estimate shown.

title: The Influence of Single Parameter Changes on Subjective Experience and Ordering Performance of Electrotactile Cues
obligation_rationale: As a psychophysics study calibrating comfortable electrotactile parameters per participant, the paper must report the delivered pulse width/frequency ranges chosen and the device's rated voltage/frequency limits (300V open-circuit, 255Hz max) separately from what participants actually experienced, since skin impedance attenuates the open-circuit voltage delivered.

title: Linear vs Logarithmic Scaling for Ordering of Electrotactile Cues
key_design_claim: Ordering three electrotactile levels was slightly better with logarithmic (19/41/68% of each person's comfortable range) than linear (25/50/75%) scaling, but not significantly; frequency levels were ordered worse than volume or pulse-width levels.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated on the palm, so the full dose is owed; per-participant calibrated pulse widths (100-2200 us) and frequencies (1-44 Hz) are given, but intensity only in device 'volume' units and the electrode only by reference to the author's prior apparatus, so current and area are unrecoverable. Recorded at the upper end of the calibrated ranges.

title: Ah-fiber nociceptive primary afferent neurons: a review of incidence and properties in relation to other afferent A-fiber neurons in mammals
obligation_rationale: This is a review of animal (mostly non-human mammal) electrophysiology on A-fiber nociceptor classification and conduction velocities; it delivers no stimulus to human participants and reports no device output specifications, so no del_* or env_* stimulation parameters are owed to the reader beyond the qualitative CV/AP property review it already provides.

title: A Wearable EMG-Driven Closed-Loop TENS Platform for Real-Time, Personalized Pain Modulation
key_design_claim: A battery-powered six-channel EMG-triggered TENS platform with a PI-controlled boost converter (up to 100 V) delivers stable biphasic output (about 22 mA) with under 10 ms closed-loop latency and about 4 h runtime at full load.
obligation_rationale: A stimulator hardware paper whose human study is still awaiting ethics approval, so it owes the device envelope: output voltage, current, programmable pulse width, rate and channels are all stated; output impedance is not.

title: Shock Me The Way: Directional Electrotactile Feedback under the Smartwatch as a Navigation Aid for Cyclists
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
key_design_claim: A nine-electrode grid under a smartwatch conveys direction: users judged it with about 19 degrees mean error for adjacent-pair cues and 23 degrees for interpolated ones, and 8 cyclists took 98.8% of junctions correctly outdoors.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated at the wrist, so the full dose is owed; waveform, pulse width, rate and the mean calibrated current (6.53 mA, SD 4.18) are stated, but the size of a single electrode is not, so charge density is unrecoverable.

title: Enhancing Presence, Immersion, and Interaction in Multisensory Experiences Through Touch and Haptic Feedback
key_design_claim: A narrative historical review of touch and haptics in entertainment and VR, distinguishing passive from actively controlled stimulation and added-on from genuinely haptic VR; electrotactile is one of six modalities covered.
obligation_rationale: A review that reports ranges across a literature rather than configurations it ran, so it carries an aggregate-envelope obligation only.

title: Closed-Loop Control of a Multifunctional Myoelectric Prosthesis With Full-State Anatomically Congruent Electrotactile Feedback
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
key_design_claim: Full-state, anatomically congruent electrotactile feedback through a forearm multi-pad electrode (biphasic, 400 us, 35-80 Hz) supported closed-loop control of a multifunctional myoelectric prosthesis in 10 non-disabled participants and one amputee.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated on the forearm, so the full dose is owed; pulse width, frequency range and waveform are stated, but amplitudes are individually calibrated without reported values and pad dimensions are not given. Recorded at the upper frequency (80 Hz).

title: Frequency Shapes the Quality of Tactile Percepts Evoked through Electrical Stimulation of the Nerves
key_design_claim: In seven amputees with implanted nerve cuffs, raising pulse frequency increased perceived frequency only up to about 50 Hz; quality was stable within 2-20 Hz and within 50-1000 Hz but differed sharply between the two ranges.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated through implanted nerve-cuff electrodes, so a non-display dose is owed; waveform (biphasic, cathodic-first, charge-balanced) and the 2-1000 Hz frequency range are stated, but per-participant amplitudes and pulse widths were not found in the extracted text. Recorded at the upper frequency.

title: Clinical Applications and Future Translation of Somatosensory Neuroprostheses
key_design_claim: Reviews somatosensory neuroprostheses that couple wearable, prosthetic or VR sensors to non-invasive or implanted nerve stimulation, arguing that the field is moving from proof-of-concept to clinical studies and setting out barriers to translation.
obligation_rationale: A review that reports ranges across a literature rather than configurations it ran, so it carries an aggregate-envelope obligation only.

title: Towards On-line Fingertip Bio-impedance Identification for Enhancement of Electro-tactile Rendering
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered stimulus envelope (sub-5mA current, 60Hz square-wave pulses, 0.454mm2 electrode area) and the identified Cole-Cole skin-electrode impedance parameters to reproduce or compare the bio-impedance identification and electro-tactile rendering calibration approach.

title: Seamlessly integrated textile electrodes and conductive routing in a garment for electrostimulation: design, manufacturing and evaluation
key_design_claim: Flat-knitted intarsia textile electrodes with knitted-in conductive leads delivered TENS charge comparably to the conductive-rubber Mollii suit, with lower skin friction and an easier fit, judged by voltage rise time, net injected charge and low-frequency contact impedance.
obligation_rationale: A textile electrode garment tested on a person with a TENS device, so the dose and interface characterisation are owed; pulse width, rate, waveform and 64 cm2 electrode area are stated, but the stimulator is voltage-controlled and current is not given.

title: An arbitrary waveform neurostimulator for preclinical studies: design and verification
obligation_rationale: This paper describes and bench/saline-tests a novel FPGA-based arbitrary waveform neurostimulator (rated ±15 V compliance, ~1 mA/V transconductance, 30 kHz bandwidth) without delivering stimulation to human participants, so readers need the device envelope (voltage compliance, channel count, bandwidth, electrode sizes tested in saline) rather than any human dosing parameters.

title: Modified pulse shapes for effective neural stimulation
obligation_rationale: This paper is a computational modeling study (no human stimulation) that owes readers the standard clinical DBS waveform parameters (200us cathodic/3ms anodic pulse widths, 15:1 amplitude ratio, 130 Hz, ~3.0V) it uses as its baseline for simulating modified pulse-shape efficiency and safety margins.

title: Preferential activation of small cutaneous fibers through small pin electrode also depends on the shape of a long duration electrical current
key_design_claim: A 50 ms bounded-exponential pulse through a 15-pin (0.2 mm) cathode gave the largest patch/pin perception-threshold ratio, i.e. the most preferential small-fibre activation; long slowly rising pulses raise large-fibre thresholds by accommodation.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated through skin electrodes, so the paper owes the full delivered dose; it states pulse durations, rate and electrode geometry but gives threshold currents only graphically, so current amplitude is unrecoverable from text.

title: A Lightweight Electrotactile Feedback Device for Grasp Improvement in Immersive Virtual Environments
obligation_rationale: Readers need the device's voltage/current ratings, channel count, and the delivered pulse width/rate/electrode geometry used with the 19 participants to replicate or compare the electrotactile grasp-feedback system, since the paper reports both a 200V/10mA-rated signal generator and specific stimulation patterns actually applied to users' fingertips.

title: The Impact of Size and Position of Reference Electrode on the Localization of Biphasic Electrotactile Stimulation on the Fingertips
key_design_claim: On an 8-pad fingertip electrode (7.0 mm2 pads, biphasic, 30 Hz), sensations spread across the fingertip but were mostly localised under the active pad, and the size and position of the reference pads shifted perceived location, a usable extra parameter.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated at the fingertip, so the full dose is owed; pad area, 30 Hz rate, biphasic waveform and pulse width are stated (printed as '400 ms', confirmed by the reviewer as 400 us), but currents only as a device range (0.1-9 mA) with individually adjusted amplitudes.

title: The ethical and regulatory landscape of wearable, ingestible, and implantable technologies in the United States
venue: Biosensing the Future: Wearable, Ingestible and Implantable Technologies for Health and Wellness Monitoring Part B
venue_key: book:biosensing the future: wearable, ingestible and implantable technologies for health and wellness monitoring part b
obligation_rationale: This is a regulatory/ethical policy review of wearable, ingestible, and implantable biosensing devices with no stimulation experiment or device specification, so it owes readers no stimulation parameters.

title: Designing Unobtrusive Modulated Electrotactile Feedback on Fingertip Edge to Assist Blind and Low Vision (BLV) People in Comprehending Charts
key_design_claim: A 1 kHz sine carrier amplitude-modulated at 40 Hz on 2 mm fingertip-edge electrodes conveyed chart shape and trajectory guidance unobtrusively; twelve blind or low-vision participants replicated line, bar and pie charts.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated at the fingertip, so the full dose is owed; waveform (1 kHz carrier, 40 Hz modulation), electrode diameter and spacing are stated, but drive is given as voltage (1 Vrms at the generator, then calibrated) and current is not reported. Recorded rate is the 40 Hz modulation.

title: Electrotactile Assistive Tools to Support Blind and Low Vision People’s Data Comprehension
key_design_claim: An adjunct overview of a research programme on fingertip-edge electrotactile tools for blind and low-vision people's data comprehension (charts, map and trip previews), reporting high pattern recognition and accurate chart replication across three twelve-participant studies.
obligation_rationale: Summarises studies that stimulated people, so a dose is owed in principle, but this short adjunct paper gives no stimulation parameters, deferring them to the full papers (e.g. Jiang2024).

title: Double-Sided Tactile Interactions for Grasping in Virtual Reality
key_design_claim: A double-sided fingertip device renders tactile cues on both thumb and index fingerpads during VR grasping; anodic pulses (200 us, 30/50 Hz, about 1.7-1.9 mA) target rapidly adapting afferents, and two-sided feedback improved grasp realism.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated at the fingertips, so the full dose is owed; mean calibrated amplitudes, pulse width, rates, anodic polarity and 2 mm electrode diameter are all stated. Recorded at 50 Hz.

title: A Novel System for Physiological Signal Monitoring and Health-Informed Electrotactile Feedback for First Responders
obligation_rationale: Since no electrotactile stimulus current, pulse width, or pulse rate delivered to human participants is reported (only device voltage/current ratings and unrelated physiological/electrochemical sensing tests), this paper cannot establish human-safe or perceptually effective stimulation parameters and only contributes device-level engineering specifications.

title: Electrotactile and vibrotactile displays for sensory substitution systems
obligation_rationale: As a review synthesizing electrode-skin interface models, sensation/pain thresholds, and safety limits from many primary studies, it owes readers the cited device envelopes (impedance, pulse width/current ranges) and thresholds as reported in the original sources, but reports no stimuli delivered to human participants in this paper itself.

title: A 16-Channel 8-Parameter Waveform Electrotactile Stimulation System
obligation_rationale: This is a hardware/engineering paper describing the ETSS device's programmable output envelope (16 channels, 0-50 mA, 0.1-25 kHz, 2-1000 us phase width, 120V compliance, 2 Mohm output impedance) and safety/charge-limiting analysis, but reports no actual human stimulation session with delivered current/timing values, so readers get device capability and safety limits rather than a per-subject dose.

title: Electrotactile Haptic Display on the Fingertips: Preliminary Results
obligation_rationale: Reports both the device's high-voltage/current capability needed to overcome fingertip skin resistance and the actual 1-10 mA, 40-100 us, 200 Hz burst-gated pulses delivered, essential for replicating fingertip electrotactile display stimulation and interpreting electrode-skin interface findings.

title: Pattern Identification on a Fingertip-Scanned Electrotactile Display
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current range, pulse width, burst timing, and electrode geometry of this 49-point fingertip electrotactile array to reproduce or compare the pattern-identification psychophysics results.

title: The Afferent Neural Response to Electrotactile Stimuli: Preliminary Results
obligation_rationale: This paper reports single-fiber primate afferent entrainment thresholds and pulse-width/polarity dependence (not human psychophysical delivery), so readers need the stimulator's compliance voltage, electrode geometry, and the pulse-width/rate protocol used to drive entrainment, but not a human dose since no human was stimulated.

title: Pattern Identification and Perceived Stimulus Quality as a Function of Stimulation Waveform on a Fingertip-Scanned Electrotactile Display
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered pulse timing (burst frequency, NPB, PRR, 50us pulsewidth, 0-6.5mA current) and electrode geometry to reproduce the psychophysical pattern-identification and quality-rating results on this 49-point fingertip electrotactile display.

title: Interaction of Perceived Frequency and Intensity in Fingertip Electrotactile Stimulation: Dissimilarity Ratings and Multidimensional Scaling
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current range (0-18.2 mA, capacitively-coupled 50-us monophasic pulses at 10-100 Hz via a 0.8 mm coaxial fingertip electrode) versus the device's rated 20 mA/510 V/8.8 Mohm output stage to distinguish participant dosimetry from instrument capability in this psychophysical dissimilarity/MDS study.

title: Tactile Feeling Display using Functional Electrical Stimulation
obligation_rationale: Reports device-rated compliance/current/rate ranges (V-I converter ±150V, 0-2mA, 0-1kHz, fixed 200us) separately from the actually delivered currents (0.2-2mA) and fixed 200Hz stimulation used to evoke RA/SAI/PC mode sensations in the single subject, so readers can distinguish hardware capability from applied dose.

title: Electrocutaneous Display with Receptor Selective Stimulations
venue: Electronics and Communications in Japan (Part II: Electronics)
obligation_rationale: The paper describes a novel receptor-selective electrotactile array design and reports the actual pulse width, current thresholds, and frequency ranges used to evoke distinct RA/SAI/PC sensations in human subjects, which are needed to reproduce and compare the psychophysical findings.

title: Optimal Design Method for Selective Nerve Stimulation and Its Application to Electrocutaneous Display
obligation_rationale: This is a theoretical/simulation paper (nerve-fiber cable model plus linear/quadratic optimization) that computes optimal waveforms for selective nerve stimulation using a phantom electrode geometry (electrodes 1mm apart, dT=10us) but never delivers current to human participants, so it owes only its modeling assumptions and simulated waveform parameters, not delivered-dose safety data.

title: Electro-Tactile Display with Tactile Primary Color Approach
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current range, fixed pulse width/rate, and 8-channel line-electrode array geometry to reproduce the tactile-primary-color stimulation and interpret the psychophysical frequency-discrimination results.

title: Electrotactile Display with Real-Time Impedance Feedback Using Pulse Width Modulation
obligation_rationale: This paper describes a real-time impedance-feedback electrotactile device and delivered 5 mA current pulses via 1.0 mm electrodes with pulse-width-modulated stimulation to 7 human participants, so both the device's 350 V/61-channel/50 Hz-refresh rated envelope and the actually delivered current/pulse-width/rate/electrode geometry must be reported separately to allow reproduction and dose comparison.

title: Electro-tactile Display: Principle and Hardware
obligation_rationale: This is a tutorial/hardware-design chapter describing typical device envelope specs (voltage source, pulse width/height ranges, electrode size and skin resistance) rather than reporting an actual human stimulation experiment, so readers need the rated design ranges to understand achievable device capability, not delivered-dose data.

title: Electro-Tactile Display Kit for Fingertip
obligation_rationale: The paper reports only device-rated envelope (300V compliance, 20mA min stable output at 10.2kΩ bench load, 7x9 electrode array at 2mm pitch) with no human stimulation session, so readers get hardware capability, not a delivered dose.

title: Electrostatic Tactile Display without Insulating Layer
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current (10 mA), pulse width (50 us), biphasic charge-balanced waveform, and 125 Hz vibration rate actually used on 8 participants, distinct from the device's rated 300 V high-voltage generator and 64-electrode bare-electrode array envelope, to assess safety margins and reproduce the electrostatic-without-insulator stimulation method.

title: Electrotactile and Electrostatic Tactile Presentation Using Bare Line Electrodes: Impact of Electrode Density
obligation_rationale: Readers need the anodic pulse parameters (80 µs, ~90 pps) and electrode pitch/gap thresholds (1.0 mm/0.5 mm) delivered in Experiment 1 psychophysics, plus the device's rated 300 V/26 mA/64-channel envelope, to compare electrotactile vs electrostatic thresholds across electrode geometries.

title: Selective electrical stimulation of low versus high diameter myelinated fibers and its application in pain relief: a modeling study
obligation_rationale: This is a purely computational modeling study (MRG myelinated fiber model, Na/K pump, dorsal horn pain circuit) with no human or animal stimulation, so no delivered-dose parameters apply; simulated HFAC frequency ranges (5-20 kHz) and derived current-amplitude equations are model outputs, not device ratings or delivered stimuli, and thus belong to neither env_* nor del_* fields in the human sense.

title: Double-sided Printed Tactile Display with Electro Stimuli and Electrostatic Forces and its Assessment
key_design_claim: A double-sided printed tactile display delivers both electrical stimulation and electrostatic friction from one sheet (50-600 V, 1-640 Hz, 1.0 mm pads); users matched stimuli across frequencies, showing the two modalities can be combined cheaply.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated at the fingertip, so the full dose is owed; it is voltage-driven (50-600 V peak, 1-640 Hz) and the pad diameter is stated, but delivered current, pulse width and participant count are not found in the text.

title: Electrodes for Transcutaneous (Surface) Electrical Stimulation
obligation_rationale: This review/experimental paper on TES electrodes reports material resistivities and a small human motor/pain threshold experiment on the forearm, but omits the specific delivered current, pulse width, and rate values, so only material and interface parameters can be extracted.

title: Indoor Walking Navigation Comparing Electrotactile Feedback with Map and Audio
key_design_claim: Directional electrotactile cues from electrode pairs on both arms and shoulders guided indoor walking navigation as well as map and audio did; navigation time did not improve, but usability ratings favoured it as an alternative.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated through skin electrodes, so the full dose is owed; pulse width and electrode size are stated, but amplitude is user-calibrated with only a 20 mA safety cap, and the standardised frequency is not given.

title: Reversible Nerve Conduction Block Using Kilohertz Frequency Alternating Current
venue: Neuromodulation: Technology at the Neural Interface
obligation_rationale: As a review of animal/preclinical KHFAC nerve block literature (no human stimulation), the paper's obligation is to accurately report the range of frequencies, amplitudes, and waveform types used across the reviewed studies (e.g., 1-100 kHz block, various Vrms/threshold values) so future researchers can standardize reporting rather than to specify any delivered human dose.

title: Characterization of an Electrode-Type Tactile Display Using Electrical and Electrostatic Friction Stimuli
obligation_rationale: Reports actual delivered current levels, pulse width, frequency range and electrode geometry used on fingerpad participants to allow replication of the combined electrical/electrostatic tactile display experiment, but does not specify the underlying device's rated output limits.

title: A tonic electrocutaneous stimulation paradigm for graded sensory C-fiber engagement in healthy subjects
key_design_claim: A personalised 60 s, 5 Hz sine-wave electrocutaneous stimulus graded at 33/67/100% of each participant's maximum gives a tonic, C-fibre-biased pain model whose intensity tracks pain ratings and skin conductance; 250 Hz and 2 kHz settings served as A-delta and A-beta controls.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated through skin electrodes, so the full dose is owed; frequencies, durations, waveform and site are given, but currents only as percentages of an individual maximum and electrode size not at all, so charge and density are unrecoverable.

title: Electrotactile Feedback Applications for Hand and Arm Interactions: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Future Directions
obligation_rationale: As a systematic review synthesizing others' work rather than delivering stimulation itself, it owes readers a clear separation between generic device/parameter guidance (e.g., electrode size, polarity, pulse width recommendations) drawn from the literature and any specific delivered doses, since no stimulus was administered to participants in this paper itself.

title: Survey on Haptic Feedback through Sensory Illusions in Interactive Systems
key_design_claim: A systematic survey of 90 papers on haptic sensory illusions in interactive systems; most use vibrotactile feedback, and only two use electrotactile feedback.
obligation_rationale: A review that reports ranges across a literature rather than configurations it ran, so it carries an aggregate-envelope obligation only.

title: WearTactile: An Electrotactile Research Platform to Support Exploration of Nuanced Electrotactile Control for Wearable Devices
obligation_rationale: This paper reports device-level ratings (voltage, current, frequency, pulse width envelopes and bench-test accuracy) for a new electrotactile hardware platform, but does not specify the exact stimulus parameters delivered during the brief n=6 user validation study, so readers get the instrument capability but not a per-participant dose.

title: Modeling of Bioimpedance for Human Skin Based on Fractional Distributed-Order Modified Cole Model
obligation_rationale: This paper reports a bioimpedance measurement (1.0 V sinusoidal, 0.1 Hz-100 kHz swept frequency, 2 cm stainless-steel electrodes 5 cm apart) used purely to fit a Cole-model equivalent circuit, not a functional electrotactile stimulus, so readers need the measurement stimulus parameters and electrode/interface details but no delivered current/pulse dosimetry exists to report.

title: Effects of Electrode Size and Spacing on Sensory Modalities in the Phantom Thumb Perception Area for the Forearm Amputees
obligation_rationale: This paper's core finding relates threshold current, pulse width/rate, and electrode diameter/spacing to sensory modality and spatial resolution, so delivered current/PW/rate/electrode geometry per size condition must be reported to let readers reproduce or compare psychophysical thresholds and TEDD outcomes.

title: Super-resolution wearable electrotactile rendering system
obligation_rationale: The paper describes a novel current-steering AC electrotactile stimulator whose device-rated voltage/frequency range (13-30V, 1Hz-100kHz, 25 channels, 4kHz refresh) and the human-delivered voltage/frequency (13-28V, 40-60Hz AM signals) must be separated so readers can distinguish device envelope from the safe stimulation actually used on volunteers.

title: TacTex: A Textile Interface with Seamlessly Integrated Electrodes for High-Resolution Electrotactile Stimulation
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current range (0.5-3mA calibrated per participant), pulse width (~200us max), electrode spacing (2mm), and body site (fingertip) alongside the device's rated envelope (up to 3mA, 350V compliance, 512x512 channels, scanning up to 250kHz) to distinguish device capability from actual human exposure.

title: ElectroClick: Enhancing Button Experiences on Surfaces with Electrotactile Sensations
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies
key_design_claim: ElectroClick gates fingertip electrotactile pulses by measured press force so a flat surface renders button clicks, keystroke granularity, frequency and patterns; frequency JND was about 22% up to roughly 200 Hz, and users matched virtual buttons to physical references.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated at the fingertip, so the full dose is owed; pulse width, frequency range and electrode diameter are stated, but current amplitudes are not (thresholds are given as compliance-voltage settings of a constant-current source meter).

title: Design and evaluation of a voltage-controlled current source for galvanic vestibular stimulation research
obligation_rationale: As a hardware/device paper delivering GVS current to human participants for JND thresholding, it must report both the device's rated output envelope (±4 mA, 24.6 V supply, 0-5kΩ target impedance) and the actual delivered stimulus (starting 1.6 mA staircase, biphasic waveform, mastoid electrodes) so readers can distinguish device capability from applied dose.

title: Coding of pleasant touch by unmyelinated afferents in humans
obligation_rationale: This study uses mechanical brush stroking (not electrical stimulation) with microneurography to characterize C-tactile and myelinated afferent firing, so it owes readers stimulus velocity/force parameters rather than electrical dose parameters, and reports no electrotactile delivery to be split into device vs delivered fields.

title: Comprehensive study of Howland circuit with non-ideal components to design high performance current pumps
obligation_rationale: This is a bench-only circuit design/characterization paper (Howland current pump for ICG) with no human stimulation, so it owes readers device envelope specs (compliance, output impedance, bandwidth, current amplitude) rather than any delivered dose parameters.

title: A multi-pad electrode based functional electrical stimulation system for restoration of grasp
obligation_rationale: Readers need delivered current (18-22 mA), pulse rate (40 Hz), and biphasic waveform used on stroke patients versus device-rated envelope (0-50 mA, 94V compliance, 1-1000 Hz, 50-1000 us) to assess safety margins and reproduce selective grasp stimulation.

title: The Impact of Stimulation Intensity on Spatial Discrimination with Multi-Pad Finger Electrode
obligation_rationale: The paper must report the delivered current range, fixed pulse width/rate, electrode pad geometry, and per-threshold amplitudes since it directly studies how stimulation intensity affects spatial localization on the finger.

title: Electrotactile Communication via Matrix Electrode Placed on the Torso Using Fast Calibration, and Static vs. Dynamic Encoding
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current range (0.6-9 mA), pulse width (300 us), frequency (50 Hz), pad geometry (8.5 mm radius, 45 mm spacing) and body site to reproduce or compare electrotactile dose applied to torso skin across studies.

title: The role of the anterolateral system in affective touch
obligation_rationale: This is a narrative/theoretical review of C-tactile afferent neurophysiology and spinal pathways with no experimental stimulation delivered to human participants, so no device or delivered-stimulus parameters are owed.

title: Charge Density and Charge Per Phase as Cofactors in Neural Injury Induced by Electrical Stimulation
obligation_rationale: This animal (feline cortex) safety-threshold study defines the charge-density/charge-per-phase injury boundary via electrode geometry, pulse waveform (400us/phase, 50Hz, 7h continuous), and area (0.002-0.5 cm2 disks; ~6.5e-5 cm2 microelectrodes), which readers need to map injury thresholds onto other electrode geometries and stimulus regimes, but no human stimulation occurred so del_* fields are not applicable.

title: Discriminative and Affective Touch: Sensing and Feeling
obligation_rationale: This is a narrative/review perspective on CT afferent neurophysiology and touch affect using mechanical (brush/stroking) stimuli, not electrotactile stimulation, and reports no device parameters or electrical stimulus delivered to participants.

title: Electrocutaneous Stimulation in a Reading Aid for the Blind
obligation_rationale: Reports comfort-optimized pulse parameters (0.5 ms, 1-200 pps) and current/voltage thresholds delivered to human fingertip subjects, needed to replicate the electrocutaneous Optacon feasibility study and its device compliance limits (1500 V source, up to 1 mA/250 V per stimulator).

title: A Miniature Programmable Multichannel Sensory Feedback Device with Electrotactile and Vibrotactile Modalities for Amputees
obligation_rationale: As a hardware paper reporting both device ratings (±5 mA, 50 V compliance, 16 channels, <10 µs response) and actual psychophysical testing (pulse widths of 50-1000 µs used to determine sensory/pain thresholds and JNDs in amputees and healthy subjects), readers need both envelope and delivered parameters kept distinct to assess device capability versus applied stimulation intensity.

title: A Sensory Feedback Neural Stimulator Prototype for Both Implantable and Wearable Applications
obligation_rationale: The paper describes a dual-mode (implantable PNS / wearable TENS) neurostimulator device, so readers need both the bench-tested rated envelope (30 channels, ±7V compliance, up to 5mA, 50-600Hz, 100-500us) and the actual TENS stimulation parameters (1-5mA biphasic pulses at 50-100Hz, 100-500us) delivered to healthy human participants to elicit somatic sensations.

title: Topics in Multiple-Loop Regulators and Current-Mode Programming
obligation_rationale: This is a power-electronics/control-theory paper on current-mode programming in switching power converters (unrelated to electrotactile stimulation of humans), so it owes no stimulation parameters at all.

title: Fractional-Order Bio-Impedance Modeling for Interdisciplinary Applications: A Review
obligation_rationale: This is a review of fractional-order bio-impedance circuit models applied to plant tissue and electrode-interface characterization, not a human stimulation study, so it owes only model/measurement parameters (frequency range, electrode type) rather than delivered stimulus dose.

title: Howland current source for high impedance load applications
obligation_rationale: This is a bench-only circuit design paper (current-source electronics for EIS) with no human stimulation; it owes only device envelope specs (transconductance, bandwidth, output impedance, supply voltage, max current 1 mAPP) since no dose was delivered to any participant.

title: Estimating nerve excitation thresholds to cutaneous electrical stimulation by finite element modeling combined with a stochastic branching nerve fiber model
key_design_claim: A layered finite-element skin model with stochastic branching fibres predicts that small electrodes concentrate current at the dermo-epidermal junction and excite A-delta before A-beta fibres; measured perception thresholds (1 ms pulses, 0.2-20 mm electrodes) followed the lowest modelled threshold.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated through skin electrodes, so the full dose is owed; pulse width, polarity and electrode diameters are stated, but thresholds only graphically, so current and density are unrecoverable. Recorded at the smallest (0.2 mm) electrode, the most demanding condition.

title: An ultrafast system for signaling mechanical pain in human skin
obligation_rationale: This paper delivers single-unit intraneural microstimulation (6.3±2.8 microA, 0.2 ms pulses, 1-300 Hz) to identified A-HTMR and A-LTMR afferents to characterize mechanical pain signaling, so it owes readers the exact microstimulation current, pulse width, and frequency range used for percept evocation.

title: Closed-loop Platform for Human Movement Augmentation with Electrotactile Feedback
obligation_rationale: Readers need delivered current, pulse parameters and electrode geometry to compare electrotactile feedback dosing across HMA closed-loop studies, but the excerpt lacks these specific delivered values.

title: A 3 MHz Low-Error Adaptive Howland Current Source for High-Frequency Bioimpedance Applications
obligation_rationale: This is a bench-tested current-source circuit design paper with resistive/RC test loads (no human stimulation), so it owes only device envelope specs (bandwidth, current range, output impedance, THD, supply voltage) rather than delivered stimulation parameters.

title: Multi Surface Electrodes Nerve Bundles Stimulation on the Wrist: Modified Location of Tactile Sensation on the Palm
key_design_claim: Combining several surface electrodes around the wrist shifts where nerve-bundle stimulation is felt on the palm, a way to steer referred tactile sensation without electrodes on the hand; current was set to 3.0 mA after thresholds peaked near that value (5 mA cap).
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated transcutaneously over wrist nerve bundles, so a non-display dose is owed; constant-current amplitude (3.0 mA, 5 mA cap) and 1 s stimulation duration are stated, but pulse width, rate, electrode size and participant count were not found in the extracted text.

title: Unmyelinated tactile afferents signal touch and project to insular cortex
key_design_claim: A patient lacking large myelinated afferents still detected slow soft-brush stroking, and fMRI showed CT-afferent input projecting to insular cortex, linking unmyelinated tactile afferents to affective touch.
obligation_rationale: Uses only mechanical (brush, vibration) and thermal stimuli, no electrical stimulation, so like other CT-afferent physiology papers it carries no dose obligation.

title: Cutaneous/Tactile Haptic Feedback in Robotic Teleoperation: Motivation, Survey, and Perspectives
key_design_claim: Surveys cutaneous and tactile feedback for robotic teleoperation by stimulus type, arguing that ungrounded cutaneous cues keep the control loop stable under contacts and delays; electrotactile cues are typically pulse trains through concentric electrodes.
obligation_rationale: A review that reports ranges across a literature rather than configurations it ran, so it carries an aggregate-envelope obligation only.

title: Wearable Haptic Feedback Interfaces for Augmenting Human Touch
key_design_claim: Reviews wearable haptic feedback interfaces by actuation principle (vibrotactile, force, thermal and electrotactile) and the materials and fabrication behind them, setting out open problems for skin-conformal haptics.
obligation_rationale: A review that reports ranges across a literature rather than configurations it ran, so it carries an aggregate-envelope obligation only.

title: C-tactile afferent stimulating touch carries a positive affective value
obligation_rationale: This is a mechanical brush-stroking study of C-tactile afferents, not electrical stimulation, so no electrical device envelope or delivered electrical stimulus parameters apply; readers need only the stroking velocity, brush width, and skin site details already given.

title: Non-monotonic kilohertz frequency neural block thresholds arise from amplitude- and frequency-dependent charge imbalance
key_design_claim: Non-monotonic kilohertz-frequency block thresholds arise from amplitude- and frequency-dependent charge imbalance (a shift toward DC block), which can let smaller fibres block at lower thresholds than larger ones.
obligation_rationale: Computational models and anaesthetised-rat experiments on implanted-cuff kHz nerve block with no human stimulation, so the paper carries no human dose obligation.

title: eTactileKit: A Toolkit for Design Exploration and Rapid Prototyping of Electro-Tactile Interfaces
obligation_rationale: This paper describes a hardware/firmware toolkit (device envelope: 0-10mA current, 270V compliance, 1-250Hz, 1us pulse-width steps, adjustable up to 10mA/2.44uA min step) but reports no human stimulation session with specific delivered parameters, so only the device's rated capability, not a delivered dose, can be extracted.

title: A High Voltage, Constant Current Stimulator for Electrocutaneous Stimulation Through Small Electrodes
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current range, pulse width, electrode diameters and monophasic waveform used on fingertip testing to compare against the device's rated 800V/25mA envelope and skin impedance model, since the paper explicitly separates device capability from actual human stimulation parameters.

title: Expert knowledge-based peak current mode control of electrosurgical generators for improved output power regulation
obligation_rationale: This is a simulation/circuit-design study of an electrosurgical generator controller tested only against simulated tissue impedance loads (10-340 ohms), with no human or animal stimulation, so it owes readers the device's rated output envelope (voltage, current, switching frequency) rather than any delivered dose.

title: Electrotactile displays: taxonomy, cross-modality, psychophysics and challenges
obligation_rationale: As a survey synthesizing device ratings, psychophysical thresholds, and safety limits from many cited studies rather than delivering stimuli itself, this paper owes readers only the aggregated parameter ranges (e.g., safe current limit, frequency tuning) it reports from the literature, not a self-generated delivered-dose envelope.

title: Research on gain scheduling
obligation_rationale: This is a control-theory survey on gain scheduling for nonlinear/LPV control systems, entirely unrelated to electrotactile stimulation, electrodes, or human dosimetry, so it owes no stimulation parameters to this meta-analysis.

title: Electrotactile Stimulation Based on Strain Energy Density of the Fingertip
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered stimulation frequency range (20-120 Hz), anodic monophasic polarity, and electrode geometry (1.25 mm diameter, 2.5 mm pitch) actually used with the 9 participants, since current amplitude and pulse width were not reported in the available text.

title: A High-Voltage Bipolar Transconductance Amplifier for Electrotactile Stimulation
obligation_rationale: This paper reports a device envelope (transconductance amplifier ratings: ±600-800V compliance, ±20mA output, 8.8MΩ output impedance, 16 channels, tested across 20-250us pulse widths and 10-100Hz pulse rates on resistive/fingertip-electrode loads) but does not deliver stimuli to human participants, so readers get engineering specifications only, not dosimetric exposure data.

title: Optimized Electrical Stimulation of C-Nociceptors in Humans Based on the Chronaxie of Porcine C-Fibers
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered pulse durations (1-250 ms half-sine), amplitudes (0.125-1.4 mA), electrode geometry (0.4 mm platinum, 2 mm spacing) and frequencies used in humans, distinct from the constant-current stimulator (DS5/DS7) capability envelope, to interpret the strength-duration/chronaxie findings and replicate the psychophysical thresholds.

title: A Finite Element Model to Identify Electrode Influence on Current Distribution in the Skin
key_design_claim: A finite-element skin model puts peak current density just under the stratum corneum beside a sweat duct; a high-resistivity electrode layer lowers that peak relative to a low-resistivity electrode, a route to more comfortable surface FES.
obligation_rationale: A computational model of current density under surface FES electrodes with no human stimulation, so it carries no dose obligation; electrode properties are modelled, not measured.

title: Skin stimulation and recording: Moving towards metal-free electrodes
key_design_claim: Metal-free laser-induced-graphene electrodes with PEDOT coatings matched Ag/AgCl for EMG recording and for electrotactile perception thresholds (DS5, 100 Hz, 250 us cathode-first charge-balanced pulses) in six participants.
obligation_rationale: Characterises an electrode and stimulates people with it, so the full dose and interface data are owed; frequency (100 Hz), pulse width (250 us), cathode-first asymmetric charge-balanced waveform, 10 mm electrode diameter and perception thresholds by stochastic-approximation staircase are stated: 0.37 mA (LIG/PEDOT) vs 0.546 mA (Ag/AgCl).

title: A model of safe levels for electrical stimulation
obligation_rationale: This paper derives a theoretical charge/charge-density safety-limit equation from prior animal (cortical) damage data (McCreery et al.) rather than delivering stimulation to human participants, so it owes readers only the model parameters (k, electrode area, pulse duration relationship) and not a delivered-dose envelope.

title: TactileWear: A Comparison of Electrotactile and Vibrotactile Feedback on the Wrist and Ring Finger
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered waveform (100 Hz biphasic pulses, 50 us pulse width, carbon-rubber electrodes 40x40mm wrist / 10x20mm ring) to reproduce this wearable notification study, though no device current/voltage envelope is disclosed since a commercial certified stimulator (Sanitas SEM 43) was used as a black box.

title: Reusable Flexible Concentric Electrodes Coated With a Conductive Graphene Ink for Electrotactile Stimulation
key_design_claim: A reusable 3D-printed concentric electrode spray-coated with graphene ink matched disposable electrodes in impedance, comfortable current range and delivered current waveform (4 mA, 100 us, 100 Hz biphasic), and still worked after 9 weeks.
obligation_rationale: Characterises an electrode and stimulates a person with it, so the full dose and interface data are owed; current, pulse width, rate, waveform and inner-electrode diameter are stated, with a single participant.

title: Compact electrotactile stimulation and EMG acquisition system with embedded blanking of stimulation artifacts
obligation_rationale: The paper describes a stimulator device with its rated envelope (0-5mA, 50-500us, 1-100Hz, 16 channels, 50V) and separately reports the specific delivered parameters (3mA, 250us, 10Hz) used in a single-subject validation test of an EMG blanking algorithm, so readers need both to distinguish device capability from actual test dose.

title: An Electrotactile Display
venue: IEEE Transactions on Man Machine Systems
obligation_rationale: As a psychophysical study delivering symmetric bipolar pulses to fingertips via a small-electrode matrix, the paper must report the delivered pulse width, repetition rate, electrode geometry, and threshold voltage/current so the described texture-sensation thresholds and JND results can be reproduced or compared across electrotactile display studies.

title: Relationship Between Pulse Rate and Pulse Width for a Constant-Intensity Level of Electrocutaneous Stimulation
obligation_rationale: A psychophysics paper deriving a PW-PR intensity matching law must report the delivered pulse widths/rates, current levels, electrode geometry and constant-current device range to allow replication of the equal-intensity contours.

title: Sensory Feedback Using Electrical Stimulation of the Tactile Sense
obligation_rationale: This is a review chapter synthesizing device design guidelines (voltage compliance, electrode area, waveform recommendations) and cited study parameters rather than reporting a new experiment delivering stimuli to participants, so readers are owed the range of typical/recommended device envelope values rather than a single delivered dose.

title: Electrical Characterisation of Aδ-Fibres Based on Human in vivo Electrostimulation Threshold
key_design_claim: Intraepidermal concentric-needle stimulation (60-1600 us single pulses, 0.05 mA steps, 2 mA cap) gave A-delta strength-duration curves with mean rheobase 0.178 mA and chronaxie 270 us; a multiscale skin and axon model attributes inter-subject spread mainly to fibre depth.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated through an intraepidermal electrode, so the full dose is owed; pulse widths and polarity are given, but threshold currents only as fitted rheobase and the electrode contact area not at all, so charge density is unrecoverable.

title: Full-hand Electro-Tactile Feedback without Obstructing Palmar Side of Hand
key_design_claim: Electrodes on the back of the hand deliver electrotactile feedback perceived across the whole hand without covering the palm, so users keep touching real objects in VR/AR; calibrated intensity averaged 1.85 mA under a 4 mA cap.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated on the hand, so the full dose is owed; mean calibrated current, pulse width (400 and 800 us) and rates (100 and 40 Hz) are stated, but electrode size and waveform polarity are not. Recorded: the 100 Hz, 400 us condition.

title: Advancing haptic interfaces for immersive experiences in the metaverse
key_design_claim: Reviews haptic interfaces for metaverse immersion across actuation types, noting that skin contamination causes impedance fluctuation in electrotactile devices and that combining electrotactile with mechanical vibration improves fidelity.
obligation_rationale: A review that reports ranges across a literature rather than configurations it ran, so it carries an aggregate-envelope obligation only.

title: Small and large cutaneous fibers display different excitability properties to slowly increasing ramp pulses
obligation_rationale: This is a human psychophysics/neurophysiology study using perception threshold tracking with ramp pulses of defined durations (1-200 ms) and specific pin/patch electrode geometries, so readers need electrode dimensions, ramp durations, and body site to interpret fiber-type-specific accommodation findings, though exact current amplitudes were adaptively titrated per subject and not fixed/reported as absolute values.

title: Exploring the Role of Electro-Tactile and Kinesthetic Feedback in Telemanipulation Task
obligation_rationale: The paper describes a multimodal (electro-tactile plus kinesthetic) telemanipulation feedback system tested on human participants, but the excerpts provide no explicit electrical stimulation parameters (current, pulse width, rate, electrode size) delivered to users, so readers are owed at minimum the missing stimulus specification to reproduce or assess safety of the electrotactile channel.

title: A portable, programmable, multichannel stimulator with high compliance voltage for noninvasive neural stimulation of motor and sensory nerves in humans
obligation_rationale: Readers need both the device's rated compliance/current envelope (±150V, 6mA, 3 channels) and the actual delivered stimulation parameters (1.2-3mA, 100-300us, 12.5-200Hz across electrocutaneous/transcutaneous/muscle/nerve targets) to reproduce or compare this noninvasive stimulator's validated human use.

title: Biocompatible, High Precision, Wideband, Improved Howland Current Source With Lead-Lag Compensation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems
obligation_rationale: This paper reports a Howland current-source circuit design for EIT with bench/SPICE-verified output impedance (3.3 Mohm up to 200 kHz) and a 1 kOhm test load, but delivers no stimulus to humans, so only device envelope specs (not delivered dose) are owed to readers.

title: The impact of walking on the perception of multichannel electrotactile stimulation in individuals with lower-limb amputation and able-bodied participants
key_design_claim: Walking raised sensation and discomfort thresholds and reduced spatial discrimination of multichannel electrotactile stimulation on the thigh compared with sitting, in 11 able-bodied participants and 6 people with lower-limb amputation, so calibration should be done in the conditions of use.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated on the thigh, so the full dose is owed; waveform, pulse width and rate are stated and thresholds are reported as group means, but pad dimensions are not given and current is reported only as thresholds, not a delivered setting.

title: Unmyelinated Afferents Constitute a Second System Coding Tactile Stimuli of the Human Hairy Skin
obligation_rationale: This microneurography study delivered brief constant-current electrical pulses (0.1 ms, up to 15 mA) via surface electrodes solely to estimate afferent conduction velocity, so readers need these delivered parameters and electrode geometry rather than any device rating, since the paper's main contribution is characterizing unmyelinated tactile afferent responses to mechanical (not electrotactile) stimuli.

title: Dynamic Impedance Model of the Skin-Electrode Interface for Transcutaneous Electrical Stimulation
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current sweep range, pulse duration, electrode sizes, and biphasic waveform used to derive the dynamic Rs/C/Ge/Gp impedance model, plus the stimulator's 110 mA compliance limit that bounded the sweep.

title: A universal model of electrochemical safety limits in vivo for electrophysiological stimulation
obligation_rationale: As a bench/in-vivo-animal electrochemical safety modeling paper with no human stimulation, it owes readers the tested current, pulse-width and impedance envelope used to derive the universal safety-limit equation, not delivered human dosimetry.

title: Design, evaluation and calibration of wearable electrotactile interfaces for enhancing contact information in virtual reality
obligation_rationale: Reports both the custom stimulator's rated envelope (0.1-9 mA, 30-500 us, 1-200 Hz, 32 channels) and the actual delivered calibration ranges/fixed parameters used per participant, essential for readers to replicate the VR electrotactile interface and its psychophysical calibration.

title: Evidence for sparse C-tactile afferent innervation of glabrous human hand skin
obligation_rationale: This microneurography study delivers only mechanical (brush stroke, monofilament, blunt tap) stimuli to characterize C-tactile afferent physiology, not electrical stimulation, so no electrical dose or device envelope parameters apply.

title: Guidelines for Snowballing in Systematic Literature Studies and a Replication in Software Engineering
obligation_rationale: This is a methodology paper on snowballing for systematic literature reviews, unrelated to electrotactile stimulation devices or human stimulation, so it owes no stimulation parameters.

title: Self-powered electrotactile textile haptic glove for enhanced human-machine interface
key_design_claim: A self-powered glove stores triboelectric charge from grasping in a capacitor and releases it through a gas-discharge tube (70-250 V breakdown) as 0.2-4.8 mA impulses; capacitance and breakdown voltage set perceived intensity (30 participants), giving battery-free electrotactile feedback.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated through hand electrodes, so the full dose is owed; impulse currents and the discharge circuit are stated, but stimulation is capacitor discharge with no defined pulse width or repetition rate, and the electrode area is not given.

title: Affective tactile comfort: is a specialized sensory system involved?
obligation_rationale: This is a journal club commentary reviewing prior CT-afferent affective touch research (brush stroking, fMRI) rather than a primary study delivering electrotactile stimulation, so no device or delivered-stimulus parameters are owed.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Electrical Stimulation Haptic Feedback in Human-Computer Interaction
obligation_rationale: As a survey aggregating parameter ranges (intensity 0-6 mA, pulse width 0-400 us, frequency 0-300 Hz) across 110 papers rather than delivering stimuli itself, it owes readers only summary ranges and citations to primary sources, not a specific device envelope or delivered-dose record.

title: A fully integrated breathable haptic textile
key_design_claim: A stretchable, breathable, bioadhesive haptic textile integrates 128 electrotactile pixels over the palm (135 V boost, monophasic 50 Hz pulses at 5% duty), keeping feedback precise under sweat and movement; 12 volunteers recognised static spatial patterns.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated on the palm, so the full dose is owed; frequency and duty cycle (pulse width 1 ms computed from the stated 50 Hz and 5%) and electrode pitch are given, but currents are individual thresholds without values and the electrode size used with participants is not stated (2, 4 and 6 mm were characterised).

title: Wearable Fabric Electrotactile System with Stimulation–Inhibition Electrode Units
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered stimulation envelope (500 Hz, 200 us pulses, 1-4 mA unipolar current via a 3x4 fabric microelectrode array with stimulation-inhibition electrode geometry) to assess how the novel electrode design's current-focusing effect translates into the reported perceptual accuracy and safety outcomes in 30 participants.

title: Leveraging deep single-soma RNA sequencing to explore the neural basis of human somatosensation
obligation_rationale: This paper delivers mechanical, thermal (QST) and brief electrical search stimuli during human microneurography to classify afferent types, so it owes readers the identified fiber types, conduction velocities and stimulus modalities used, but it reports no programmable electrical stimulator envelope since electrical pulses (0.4 ms) were used only to locate/confirm units, not as a parameterized therapeutic stimulus.

title: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy Increases Electrical Stimulation Threshold of Sciatic Nerve: A Prospective Parallel Cohort Study
venue: Diabetes, Metabolic Syndrome and Obesity: Targets and Therapy
obligation_rationale: Readers need the delivered current threshold range, pulse width, and rate used to elicit motor responses via percutaneous nerve stimulation to compare stimulation-threshold findings across diabetic and control cohorts, since no device output envelope (rated max current/compliance) is reported for the clinical nerve stimulator used.

title: Evaluation of multiple perceptual qualities of transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for evoked tactile sensation in forearm amputees
key_design_claim: Small (10 mm) TENS electrodes over the projected finger map of the forearm stump consistently evoked vibration (20 Hz) and buzz (50 Hz) sensations; pulse-width JNDs were about 13-15 us, and buzz coding let five amputees identify finger contact with 77% accuracy.
obligation_rationale: Humans were stimulated transcutaneously on the forearm stump, so a non-display dose is owed; waveform, frequencies and 10 mm electrode diameter are stated, but amplitudes are set per site and pulse width is the varied variable, without a single delivered value. 5 amputees and 14 able-bodied subjects.

title: Electrotactile Perception Properties and Its Applications: A Review
obligation_rationale: As a review synthesizing perceptual and device parameters across many primary studies (thresholds, waveform, frequency, electrode siting) without delivering stimuli itself, it owes readers accurate attribution of which parameter ranges and device envelopes came from which cited source rather than its own dosimetry.

title: Explore Electrotactile Parametric Properties Using an Electrical Stimulation System
obligation_rationale: The paper describes a custom 6-channel constant-current stimulator (rated up to 5mA at 90V compliance, load-tested to 18k ohm) and reports the actual delivered parameters (PA 0.1-3mA, PW 100-2000us, PF 5-80Hz, 10mm hydrogel electrodes) used in psychophysical threshold and JND experiments on 8 subjects, so readers need both the device envelope and delivered stimulus values to reproduce or compare the sensory results.
